newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Wheat contracts to sell again on Belgrade bourse.
newsitem.headline: Wheat contracts to sell again on Belgrade bourse.

text.p: Serbia's Commodity Reserve Agency will continue to sell its wheat contracts via the Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) next week, no longer accepting payment by instalments, the bourse said on Wednesday.
Economists said the move by the Commodity Reserve Agency was clearly signalling that Serbia's government and its bodies were not convinced themselves about future inflation and the dinar stability.

"They know more they we do, but if they stop accepting payment by instalments it's an almost clear signal what will happen to prices and the dinar pretty soon," said an economist, who spoke under condition of anonymity.

The agency will offer a new tranche of contracts, selling little over 183,000 tonnes of wheat for a total of 165 million dinars ($30.03 million), but will accept only payments in full, head of BSE clearing department Tihomir Podunavac told Reuters.
The contract's face value remains unchanged at 9,000 dinars with 10 tonnes of wheat sold as collateral and a 32 percent discount. It also provides its holder with an export licence.
Analysts said it was difficult to explain the decision to abandon payment by instalments.

"Amidst pronounced illiquidity in the entire economy, they decide not to retain the only attractive bit which sold the contracts. It was easier for flour mills to plan payments in four instalments," an analyst said.
Serbia began raising funds to finance the 1997 wheat sowing last October. Since then, it sold 47,530 tonnes of wheat out of 165,000 tonnes offered.
Market analysts said keeping maturity of the previous tranche unchanged at August 31, meant maturity was getting shorter opening some space for speculators to enter the game.

"But real interest from speculators (banks) could be expected only if the sale continues in April and May. That would open some space for those investors, currently facing serious liquidity problems," an analyst said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
